title: How Learning to Read Changes Lives

blanks.sentence: Reading helps with ordinary tasks, such as checking product _____ while shopping.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Why literacy matters

blanks.sentence: A UN report estimates that _____ adults worldwide cannot read or write.
In coastal towns, regular _____ forces families to move, making school difficult for children.
The Friendship Project teaches reading and writing to _____.
Before learning to write, one learner used her _____ instead of signing her name.
At Readeasy, trained volunteers teach adult learners _____, rather than in groups.
One learner who could not read before is now working through the _____.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the opening discussion describe reading as an essential skill?
options: It allows people to follow printed information used in everyday life.
It enables people to finish journeys to work more quickly.
It helps people choose which news reports are most reliable.
It helps people judge product quality without asking shop staff.

multipleChoice.question: What is presented as the main reason many people grow up unable to read, with coastal Bangladesh given as an example?
options: Their families prefer lessons at home to formal classes.
They do not attend school, sometimes because moving disrupts education.
Their schools concentrate on counting rather than reading.
They begin work before they have learnt to write their names.

multipleChoice.question: How did Rashida say her children reacted to her inability to read and write?
options: They were worried that she would stop keeping household accounts.
They were relieved that she could already sign official papers.
They felt embarrassed that their mother could not read or write.
They became interested in joining her lessons themselves.

multipleChoice.question: What does the Bangladeshi learner's account suggest about managing her money after the lessons?
options: She can work out in advance what every purchase will cost.
She can provide financial advice to other learners.
She now relies on her children to record her expenses.
She can make informed checks that may protect her from being cheated.

multipleChoice.question: How is the English project presented in relation to the Bangladeshi one?
options: It serves a different country where adults also face literacy difficulties.
It offers the same group lessons to women and girls in coastal towns.
It is described as replacing the Bangladeshi project's approach.
It serves adults who already read but need help with maths.

multipleChoice.question: How did Peter's childhood hearing difficulties affect his education, according to the discussion?
options: They led his family to keep him away from school.
They caused him to lose interest in learning after school.
They made it harder for him to keep up at school, and he did not learn to read.
They meant that he learnt reading only through written college lessons.

multipleChoice.question: How did the unsuccessful college attempts affect Peter's belief about learning to read?
options: He thought independent reading was unnecessary once a neighbour could help.
He thought the college courses had prepared him to read letters.
He blamed only his hearing difficulties for the unsuccessful courses.
He had begun to doubt that learning to read would work for him.

multipleChoice.question: What does Peter's later reading of the Harry Potter books most clearly illustrate?
options: The books were the teaching materials used in every Readeasy lesson.
The lessons have enabled him to read for himself after earlier difficulties.
His childhood hearing problems have now completely disappeared.
He has finished all the books since joining Readeasy.
